title: The ULTIMATE Chest Exercises Tier-List (Gorilla-tier to A cup-tier)
summary: NH ranks about 60 chest exercises from Gorilla tier to A-cup tier, prioritizing the lower and mid chest and the shoulder cost. Gorilla tier: bench press, low-to-high cable fly, dips, ring push-ups, converging chest press, Spoto press, dumbbell press, fly press, plate-loaded press and cambered bar bench. Gimmicks like plate presses, Svend presses, Swiss-ball presses and floor flies go to the bottom.
claims: Ranking criteria: the lower and mid chest make up most of the muscle's mass and look, so a lift that only builds the upper chest can never be top tier; shoulder involvement also counts
NH built his chest mainly with the bench press and push-ups, without fancy methods
Bench press is Gorilla tier; if bench works for you, keep benching
Larsen press is excellent: instability and no leg drive train you differently but remove the stability that lets you grind reps
Leg drive helps the bench by creating stability, not by magically adding force
Swiss-ball press is A-cup tier: an unstable back surface makes scapular retraction, which protects the shoulders and keeps the chest engaged, harder
Push-ups are excellent: many built big chests from high-volume bodyweight push-ups, but range is limited by the floor and they can tax the wrists
Diamond push-ups are decent for chest because elbow flexion shifts work to triceps; Pike push-ups are mediocre because they are mostly shoulders
Low-to-high cable fly is Gorilla tier, his top cable fly: stretch behind the body with bent elbows, easy squeeze, 15 reps for 4 sets with low fatigue
High-to-low cable fly is excellent; mid-level cable fly is only decent because a lying dumbbell fly can replicate it
Straight-arm pec deck is mediocre: a longer lever forces less weight and shifts stress to the shoulder; the bent-arm pec deck is excellent
Flies complement presses; if a fly taxes your shoulders enough to hurt your pressing, you are doing something wrong
Dips are Gorilla tier, arguably better than bench in some ways for stretch and range, but growing young men should watch for sternum or rib cage pain
Decline (feet-elevated) push-up is excellent; weighted deficit push-up gives full control of hand position and full stretch
Ring push-ups are Gorilla tier: the rings can rotate, they spare the wrists, allow more range and let the shoulder blades retract
Ring flies are excellent but risky; build up from neutral-grip ring push-ups by gradually widening the arms to avoid tearing a pec or rotator cuff
Chest press machines that diverge outward and upward are mediocre, really shoulder presses; converging chest presses are Gorilla tier
Upright horizontal presses complement lying presses the way cable rows complement bent-over rows
The steeper the incline, the more shoulder work; a heavy flat press immediately followed by a heavy incline press makes the two compete
If you do incline presses, treat them as a priority lift, not an afterthought
Reverse-grip barbell bench is mediocre: awkward on the wrists, only a little more upper chest; reverse-grip dumbbell press is excellent because each hand is independent
The Power Twister is A-cup tier: little real stimulus beyond sensation; chest expanders are mediocre for chest but great for back and arms
Close-grip bench is excellent but often limited by the triceps and has less elbow flare; better to prioritize it over the Larsen press as the main chest accessory
Flaring the elbows is how you recruit more chest, even if it is now seen as dangerous
Spoto press is Gorilla tier: pausing just above the chest spares the shoulders and keeps the chest in a stretch; touch-and-go bench hurt NH's shoulders over time
Football (neutral grip) bar bench is excellent; athletes and linemen should press this way for sport specificity
Plate press is A-cup: it becomes a grip exercise with no stretch; the standing Svend press does not even load the chest because gravity pulls down
Dumbbell press is Gorilla tier and underrated; anyone who does not feel bench in the chest should start with dumbbells
NH stopped dumbbell pressing because his heavy home dumbbells are too bulky and hit his chest
Alternating dumbbell press is only decent: no reason to stretch one side at a time when lying on a bench
Arnold press is mediocre and overhead press is A-cup for chest; these are shoulder lifts
Hindu push-up is mediocre, planche push-up decent, one-arm push-up A-cup: advanced calisthenics skills are not what builds the muscle, the basic training to get there is
Straight-arm dumbbell flies are only decent; fly presses are Gorilla tier, giving the same stretch and squeeze with more weight and safety
Incline dumbbell bench cable fly is excellent: the incline stops overextension and pushes you toward a fly press
Floor press is only decent because the floor blocks the full stretch; floor fly is A-cup
Medicine ball chest press and medicine ball push-ups are A-cup; clap push-ups are only decent, add weight instead
Landmine press is A-cup and Viking press mediocre: the more you press in front of you, the more chest
Plate-loaded converging bench machines are Gorilla tier (he corrected himself on placement); some may even beat the bench
Upper chest shrug (Michael Gundill) is decent: great stimulus-to-fatigue ratio for upper chest without pressing
Guillotine press is excellent with submaximal loads and a spotter; NH prefers it on rings
Cambered bar bench is Gorilla tier: it lets the elbows and hands go deeper for extra stretch
Band-resisted push-ups are excellent for overloading push-ups without a vest; crucifix push-ups are mediocre
Crossing the arms past each other on cable crossovers adds shoulder and upper back work, not chest; the hands touching is maximum contraction
Smith machine press is excellent for advanced lifters but a bad starting point for beginners
Wall push-ups provide almost no tension; beginners should do incline or knee push-ups
Pullover is mediocre for chest: the chest feels a passive stretch from the shoulder position, which can be risky to overload
Hex/squeeze press is decent; seated cable chest press is excellent, standing versions are A-cup because people cheat with the body
